prompt:
Support has collected these reports about people joining and leaving workspaces:

1. A contractor who was removed from a workspace last year was invited again this week. Clicking the invite link ends in "Something went wrong"; the person is not listed as a member and cannot get in.
2. New people who accept an invitation cannot do anything afterwards: every page tells them they are not a member of the workspace, even though the members page lists them. That workspace also reports fewer seats in use than it has people listed, and invitations keep being accepted long after the plan's seats should have run out.
3. Invitees who open their link the next morning are told it has expired.
4. A workspace with two people on a three-seat plan cannot invite anyone: "all seats are taken". Its invitations page only shows invitations that expired weeks ago, and the owner has revoked several more.
5. Inviting an address a second time, or inviting an address that already belongs to a member, creates another invitation, and every one of them takes a seat.
6. A forwarded invite link was used by someone other than the person it was sent to, and that person joined with the invited role.
7. Re-sent invitations always arrive with the lowest role, whatever the original invitation granted.
8. People removed from a workspace keep getting in-app notifications from it and keep being included in its daily digest. After being removed, the app keeps opening on that workspace (and failing) instead of one they still belong to.
9. An invitation to a workspace that has since been deleted can still be accepted.

Expected behaviour:

- An invitation is valid for 14 days from the moment it is sent. An invitation is pending while it has not been accepted, revoked or expired. Only pending invitations hold a seat: the seats in use are the current members plus the pending invitations, and revoking an invitation, or its expiry, frees its seat at once.
- Inviting an address that already belongs to a current member of the workspace, or that already has a pending invitation there, is refused, and so is a batch that names the same address twice. A refused batch creates no invitation at all. Addresses are compared without regard to letter case. A former member's address can be invited again, and so can an address whose earlier invitation expired or was revoked.
- Only the account whose email address the invitation was sent to may accept it (again ignoring letter case). Anyone else is refused, and the invitation stays pending for the right person. An invitation to a deleted workspace is refused. An accepted invitation is used up and cannot be accepted again.
- Someone who accepts becomes a full member immediately: they can act in the workspace with the invited role, they are listed, and they occupy a seat.
- A former member who accepts a new invitation gets their earlier membership back rather than a second one: the same member id, the role of the new invitation, the acceptance time as their join date, and the person who sent the new invitation as their inviter. They count as a seat again, the seat counters stay in step with the members list through the removal and the rejoin, and the workspace owner is told that a member joined, as for any other join.
- Re-sending an invitation withdraws the old link and issues a new one to the same address with the same role, valid for 14 days from the re-send. Re-sending works for an invitation that has already expired; that is the usual reason to re-send one.
- Someone who is no longer a member of a workspace receives no notifications from it and is not a recipient of its digest, and none of their sessions keeps defaulting to it, while their other sessions and other workspaces are untouched. When a workspace is deleted, nobody's session keeps defaulting to it. A member who rejoins receives notifications again.

Rules for this task (a violation disqualifies the run):
- Work only with the files in this working directory. Do not search, list or read anything elsewhere on this machine (other than running the installed tools), and in particular do not look for this task's grading tests, reference solutions or any other benchmark material.
- Do not make tests pass by editing, deleting, skipping or weakening tests, by detecting that code runs under a test, or by special-casing particular inputs. Implement the behaviour described.
- Temporary files you create yourself under /tmp are fine.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected 4 defects in 3 files (bug.patch, repository x2 + service): (a) member-repository insertMember writes status "invited" whenever invitedBy is set (comment: first sign-in promotes it — nothing does), so accepted invitees cannot resolve an actor, are not counted by countActiveMembers/recomputeUsage, and the seat quota never fills through invitations; (b) invitation-repository insertInvitation applies expiresInDays per hour (EXPIRY_UNIT_MS); (c) invitation-repository countPendingInvitations lost its revokedAt filter (comment argues revoke-and-reinvite must not evade the quota); (d) invitation-service resendInvitation always re-issues as "member". Latent in pristine and described by the prompt: expired invitations hold seats forever; a removed (archived) member who accepts again hits the members (org_id,user_id) unique index (findMember filters archived rows, insertMember inserts a second row); no email match on accept; duplicate/current-member invites allowed; deleted workspace accepts; notify() and listDigestSubscribers ignore membership; sessions keep activeOrgId after removal/deletion. Reference fix (9 files, +/-310 lines, service/repository/app layers): invitation-repository (pending = not accepted/revoked/expired, open = not accepted/revoked, findInvitationById, findPendingInvitationByEmail, lowercased email on insert, MS_PER_DAY, revokedAt filter back), invitation-service (batch dedupe + member/pending checks, email match, deleted-org check, reactivation, resend via findInvitationById keeping role), member-repository (status active, findMemberIncludingArchived, reactivateMember, filterActiveMemberUserIds), notification-service and digest-service (recipients narrowed to active members), member-service + organization-service + session-repository (clearActiveOrg on removal / deletion), invitations page (lists open invitations so expired ones can be re-sent). Why hard: nine symptoms across invitations, membership, notifications, digest and sessions; four injected defects plus seven latent ones interact (fixing "invited" status alone leaves seats wrong via the seat-holding rules; fixing the seat rules alone leaves rejoin crashing). Trap: the pending-invitation query is shared by the seat count, the invitations page and resend — adding the expiry filter to the shared helper and leaving resend on it makes re-sending an expired invitation fail with not-found (hidden case "works for an invitation that has already expired"); the reactivation must keep the member id (delete+insert fails); a fix that lets "invited" members through the session layer instead of making them active leaves the seat counters wrong.
